help.heading: How to build a query
help.intro: Everything you pick becomes SQL in the panel on the right.
help.columns_text: Click the circle at the end of a field on the diagram, or right-click the field and choose Add to query. Fields of several tables are joined along the links between them.
help.join_text: Drag a primary key (PK) onto the field of another table that refers to it - or click one, then the other, or right-click the field → Link to. Queries join the tables on the link, and it is saved as a foreign key at the next Run. To join on other fields, or keep the rows without a match (LEFT JOIN), use {add_join} in the query panel: that changes nothing in the database.
help.summarize_text: Click a column in the query panel, then SUM, AVG, COUNT, COUNT UNIQUE, MIN or MAX in the toolbar (or use the pill on the column). Every column you do not summarize becomes a group - GROUP BY is written for you. Count rows adds how many rows each group has.
help.filter_text: Right-click a field and choose Add filter…, pick how to compare and type the value as it is - no quotes. A filter on a summarized column can test each group instead of each row (HAVING). Click a filter in the panel to change it.
help.sort_text: The arrow on a column sorts by it: smallest first, largest first, off. Limit keeps the first rows; Distinct shows each different row once.
help.run_text: {run_query} or {keys}. The SQL can be edited by hand before it runs; it is only written over when you change the query on the diagram.
